extra.message: ApiKey Model Lacks Expiration — Permanent Non-Expiring Keys

metadata.citation:
class ApiKey(models.Model):
    label = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    prefix = models.CharField(max_length=16, unique=True)
    key_hash = models.CharField(max_length=64, unique=True)
    active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    created_by = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, related_name="created_api_keys")
    last_used_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
metadata.proof: The ApiKey model definition contains no expires_at or valid_until field. ApiKey.issue() (models.py:469) creates keys with no expiration timestamp. ApiKey.authenticate() (models.py:479) filters only on prefix + active=True with no expiry check. The sole revocation path is manual admin toggle via api_key_toggle view. Once issued, keys remain valid indefinitely. If a key is leaked, stolen, or an integration is decommissioned without manual deactivation, the key grants perpetual access to the availability API and any future API-key-protected endpoints.
